outlet: News From The States - Fair. Fearless. Free.
headline: Democrats more trusted on healthcare costs, survey shows
summary: Democrats lead in voter enthusiasm and trust on healthcare and abortion issues, but Republicans have an edge on immigration. A majority favors a national health plan, though support fluctuates based on how it's framed. Voters want healthcare system changes, with nearly 9 in 10 seeking major or complete overhauls.

headline: How the Scarborough ICE facility is feeding the nationwide detention apparatus
summary: ICE detentions at Scarborough facility in Maine have increased under Trump's second term, with more overnight stays and rapid transfers out of state, raising concerns about legal representation and detention conditions.

headline: Poll: Moore sits with a comfortable 2-1 margin over Republican challenger Cox
summary: A UMBC poll shows Maryland Gov. Wes Moore (D) leading Republican nominee Dan Cox 51% to 24% ahead of their Oct. 6 debate, reflecting Cox's conservative image and lack of moderate appeal.

headline: Supporters of Barrett, Lawrence clash at dueling protests ahead of debate
summary: Supporters of Democratic nominee Will Lawrence and incumbent Republican Rep. Tom Barrett clashed in downtown Lansing in separate protests ahead of their upcoming congressional debate. Lawrence supporters criticized Barrett's record on AI, healthcare, and other issues, while Barrett's supporters targeted Lawrence's associations with democratic socialists and his protest history. Both protests reflect the increasing polarization and tension leading up to the 2026 general election.

headline: For U-M pro-Palestinian protesters, consequences linger after charges were dropped
summary: Pro-Palestinian activists at U-M faced repercussions including arrests, disciplinary actions, and job losses after protests; despite charges being dropped, activists argue university and government actions targeted their political beliefs and criminalized protest.

headline: Child dies from bacterial infection, state health department reports
summary: A Montana child died last month from complications of Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), prompting the state health department to remind parents to keep their children up-to-date on Hib vaccinations, which have significantly reduced Hib cases since 1987. Montana has recorded four other pediatric deaths since 2012 due to invasive H. influenzae, none of which were identified as type b. Hib vaccine is recommended for all children under five years old, with older children and adults only requiring it if they have certain medical conditions. The tragedy underscores the importance of public health efforts in maintaining vaccination rates to protect vulnerable populations.

headline: Montana health officials warn of severe risks as Fergus County confirms measles case
summary: Montana has seen six measles cases this year, with Fergus County confirming a case this month. Declining vaccination rates pose a risk to Montanans, with Montana's rate at 86.3%. Governor Gianforte signed a bill in 2021 restricting health departments' access to student immunization records.

headline: South Dakota National Guard helps with more than 1,000 deportations since July 2025, governor says
summary: South Dakota's Governor Rhoden extends cooperation with ICE for paperwork processing until 2027, with 1,013 deportations processed since July 2025. State agencies have 287(g) agreements with ICE, involving 11 agencies, including Highway Patrol and corrections. This cooperation has led to 261 immigration-related arrests and parole of 38 inmates into ICE custody. Centerville Police Chief hopes agreement helps secure federal grant funding.

headline: Arkansas lawmakers adopt recommendations for per-student school funding
summary: The Arkansas Joint Education Committee recommended a 2.4% increase in per-student funding for public schools over two years, reaching $8,431 in 2028. The increase includes $26 million for dyslexia intervention and $14 million for high-cost special needs funding. Lawmakers requested more time for discussion before voting on the recommendations, which will be considered during the legislative session starting in January.

headline: Lamont touts CT response to Medicaid cuts, stops short of pledging funds
summary: Connecticut's Medicaid program, HUSKY D, faces federal work requirements starting Jan. 1, potentially impacting around 108,000 residents. Governor Ned Lamont, while advocating for residents, refrained from committing state funds to offset potential federal cuts, stating, "I’d like to see the feds step up and do what their piece of the responsibility is." The state is working to verify eligibility and ensure exemptions, with a focus on "medically frail" individuals. The article does not directly discuss the state budget, but the potential loss of federal funding for Medicaid could have budgetary implications for Connecticut.

headline: Republican gubernatorial nominee Gregg Hull announces plan to phase out New Mexico’s income tax
summary: New Mexico gubernatorial nominee Gregg Hull proposed a phased plan to eliminate the state's personal income tax over four years. This plan aims to reduce poverty and wealth disparity without introducing new taxes or cutting programs, but relies on legislator approval and maintaining a minimum general fund reserve of 25% of current expenses.

headline: ‘A political prisoner’: Roebling Bridge ICE protestor now faced with felony charge, arrested
summary: A year after protests at Roebling Bridge over immigration officials' actions, Kentucky protester Taylor Marshall was rearrested and charged with felony riot, raising concerns about delayed prosecutions and potential political motivations.

headline: 58,000 Hoosiers not in compliance with new HIP work rules
summary: Up to 58,000 Indiana Medicaid recipients may lose coverage due to new federal work requirements taking effect Jan. 2027, potentially impacting public health by reducing access to care for vulnerable populations.

headline: Judge dismisses Trump administration lawsuit over West Orange synagogue protest
summary: A federal judge dismissed claims against pro-Palestinian protesters sued by the Trump administration under a federal statute meant to prevent obstruction of religious observances, ruling the government failed to allege a claim under the act. The ruling may set a precedent for future protests, clarifying the bounds of protected speech and assembly.

headline: New polling shows Morrisey at 31-45% approval; it could affect Republican candidates this fall
summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey's approval ratings are underwater in West Virginia, potentially impacting Republican candidates in tight statehouse races. A poll by State Navigate showed 61% disapproval in Kanawha County's Senate District 8 and an even 45-45 split in the Northern Panhandle's Senate District 1. The poll also found that a Morrisey endorsement could be toxic in District 8, with 45% of respondents less likely to vote for an endorsed candidate.

headline: Mississippi agencies ask for more money as lawmakers begin work on $7B budget
summary: Mississippi agencies requested increased budgets for FY2028, totaling over $7 billion. Key requests include IHL's $93M increase, MEMA's $70M request due to disasters, Medicaid's $179M increase, and CPS's $52M rise. The Joint Legislative Budget Committee will issue recommendations and revenue estimates later this year, with the final budget set during the regular legislative session in January.

headline: After years of problems, Alaska plans to outsource payroll for 14,000 public employees
summary: The Alaska Department of Administration plans to outsource state employee payroll to a private company by 2027, potentially displacing up to 14,000 workers. This decision aims to address chronic staffing issues and reduce payroll errors, with the state prepared to spend $4 million annually for the service. The move could save the state around $6 million annually, potentially impacting the state budget. Unions have raised concerns about job losses and increased costs.
